lead.label: (R)-3t
lead.why: Abstract: 'we identified a potent and reversible MAGL inhibitor, compound (R)-3t. Oral administration of compound (R)-3t to mice decreased AA levels and elevated 2-AG levels in the brain.'

target.name: (R)-1-[3-Fluoro-5-(2-methylpyridin-3-yl)phenyl]-4-[4-(pyrimidin-2-yl)piperazin-1-yl]pyrrolidin-2-one (racemate; the (R) enantiomer is separated by chiral HPLC, not a reaction)

reactions.conditions: Michael addition: piperazine and 2(5H)-furanone in MeOH, 0 C to rt, overnight (procedure of 9a: 'similar procedure'); 85%.
reactions.source: Scheme 2 (a); Experimental, 9a procedure and 9b ('similar procedure to 9a', 85%)

reactions.conditions: Aluminium-mediated lactone aminolysis: aniline, DABAL-Me3, toluene, 80 C, 1 h (procedure of 10b); 73%. The aniline is not named in the text; derived from the product name 10d.
Intramolecular Mitsunobu cyclisation (amide N-alkylation): ADDP, tri-n-butylphosphine, THF, 0 C to rt, overnight (procedure of 3i); 65%.
Suzuki-Miyaura coupling: boronic acid, (A-taPhos)2PdCl2, Cs2CO3, toluene/water, 100 C, microwave (procedure of 3l); 78%. The boronic acid is not named in the text; derived from the product structure.

notes: No SI file. Counted as 4 chemical reactions (steps 1-4) plus one chiral separation (step 5, not a reaction); if a reviewer counts the resolution, the route is 5 and the paper must be excluded as over 4. Stereo-SMILES (R) derived by hand: [C@@H] in the written order (CH2C=O, H, N-piperazine, CH2N) is R (priorities N > CH2N > CH2C=O > H). Aniline and boronic acid reagents are inferred from product names, not printed. Substrate 1-(pyrimidin-2-yl)piperazine is not named (procedure by analogy with 9a, whose piperazine is named); the paper says all reagents are from commercial sources. The stereocentre arises only at step 1 (racemic). | EDITED 2026-10-24: step 5 (chiral HPLC resolution) removed, target is the racemate.
